hook: The Nazi dictator who started the Second World War in Europe and ordered the Holocaust.

pages.x: Adolf Hitler was born in 1889 in Braunau am Inn, Austria, the son of a customs officer. He was twice turned down by the art academy in Vienna, and lived there in poverty, selling pictures he copied from postcards, and taking in the hatred of Jews in the city's politics.
He served as a messenger in the German army and was gassed. He blamed Germany's defeat on Jews and Marxists, spreading the lie that the army had been "stabbed in the back".

In Munich he took over a small far-right party, the Nazis. In 1923 he tried to seize power in a coup that failed. In prison he wrote Mein Kampf, full of hatred for Jews and plans to conquer land in the east.

The Great Depression brought the Nazis millions of votes. In January 1933 Hitler was made chancellor. Within months he had banned all other parties, opened the first concentration camps and made himself dictator.
The Nuremberg Laws of 1935 stripped Jews of their rights as citizens. On Kristallnacht, in November 1938, mobs burned synagogues and smashed Jewish shops and homes across Germany.

He rearmed Germany, took Austria and Czechoslovakia, and on 1 September 1939 invaded Poland, starting the Second World War in Europe. By 1941 his armies had conquered most of Europe, and then invaded the Soviet Union.

In the Holocaust the Nazis murdered six million Jews, two of every three in Europe, in mass shootings and in death camps such as Auschwitz. They also murdered millions of others: Roma, disabled people, Poles and Soviet prisoners.

After defeats at Stalingrad and in Normandy, the Allied armies closed in. On 30 April 1945, with Soviet troops fighting in the streets of Berlin, he killed himself in his bunker. Germany surrendered a week later.
Hitler started the deadliest war in history, in which some 70 to 85 million people died, and ordered the Holocaust. Germany today teaches this history so that it can never happen again.
